The Automated Scholarship Records Management System was developed to make the scholarship process in the Local Government Unit of San Enrique faster, more organized, and easier to manage. Before the system was created, scholarship applications were handled mostly through manual recording, paper-based submissions, and repeated checking of documents. Because of this, staff had to spend more time sorting records, tracking applicant progress, and updating statuses, while students had limited ways to monitor their applications.

To solve these problems, the researchers created a web-based system that simplifies the scholarship process from application up to payout scheduling. Students can register, fill out their application online, upload requirements, submit their digital signature, track their status, and receive notifications about updates such as document review, interview schedules, Statement of Account (SOA) submission, and payout schedules. On the other hand, staff and administrators can verify documents, schedule interviews, process SOA submissions, manage payouts, post announcements, and generate reports more efficiently.
With the system in place, scholarship records can be handled in a more accurate, secure, and organized way. It helps

manual work, avoids repetitive tasks, improves transparency, and provides a more convenient experience for both applicants and LGU personnel. Overall, the system serves as a practical solution for improving scholarship management in the municipality.

This study focuses on the design, development, and implementation of a web-based Automated Scholarship Records Management System for the Local Government Unit (LGU) of San Enrique, Negros Occidental. The system is intended to support and improve the existing scholarship management process by providing a centralized platform for applicant registration, online scholarship application, document upload, application status tracking, applicant and scholar record management, interview scheduling, and notification delivery through SMS with One-Time Password (OTP) mobile number verification. It also includes features for monitoring application progress, managing scholarship-related announcements, organizing submitted records, and recording scholarship disbursement details for documentation and tracking purposes.

The system is designed for use by scholarship applicants, LGU staff, and scholarship coordinators of the Municipality of San Enrique. Its main purpose is to improve efficiency, organization, accessibility, and communication in handling scholarship records and applicant information. Specifically, it reduces reliance on
manual record-keeping and supports faster dissemination of updates such as application results, interview schedules, and payout-related announcements.

However, the system is limited to records management, monitoring, and notification functions only. It does not replace government-mandated and office-based procedures such as the physical submission of required documents, actual document verification, accounting review, auditing, final approval by authorized personnel, and the actual release of scholarship funds. Uploaded documents in the system are intended only for digital submission, pre-screening, and reference, while official validation may still require physical copies and manual checking by the responsible offices.

The study is further limited by the accuracy and completeness of the data provided by users, the availability and stability of internet connectivity, and the reliability of third-party SMS services for OTP and notification delivery. In addition, the system does not provide real-time chat or direct messaging between applicants and LGU personnel, since communication is limited to system-generated and SMS-based notifications. Lastly, the system is developed specifically for the scholarship procedures of the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental, and is not intended for direct implementation in other LGUs without further modification and customization.

To ensure the successful adoption of the Automated Scholarship Records Management System for the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental, the researchers plan to conduct a structured implementation process. This process will begin with an orientation and hands-on training session for the intended users of the system, particularly the scholarship staff, coordinators, and authorized LGU personnel. The training will cover user account access, applicant record management, document monitoring, interview scheduling, status updating, notification handling, and basic troubleshooting procedures. User guides and instructional materials will also be provided to help users become familiar with the system’s functions and navigation.

The researchers plan to implement the system through a phased roll-out approach. In the initial phase, the system will be deployed for pilot use within the scholarship office to allow selected staff and coordinators to test its core functions, such as applicant registration, application review, document tracking, and SMS-based notification delivery. Feedback gathered during this phase will be used to identify necessary adjustments and improvements before full implementation. After successful pilot testing, the system will be fully deployed for regular use in managing scholarship applications and records within the LGU. Throughout the
rollout period, the researchers will provide technical assistance to address user concerns and ensure smooth operation.

Upon full implementation, the researchers will establish a maintenance and monitoring plan to sustain the performance and reliability of the system. This will include routine database backup, system updates, correction of identified errors, and continuous monitoring of usability and functionality. A designated system administrator or authorized LGU personnel will oversee the regular operation of the system, including user account management, record monitoring, and coordination of technical concerns. Through this implementation plan, the researchers aim to ensure that the system will be effectively adopted and maintained as a reliable tool for scholarship records management in the LGU of San Enrique.

The Automated Scholarship Records Management System was tested to determine whether it performs according to its intended functions and requirements. The testing process focused on verifying the accuracy, reliability, usability, and security of the system in handling scholarship-related transactions. Specifically, the researchers examined whether the system could properly manage applicant registration, login with OTP verification, scholarship application submission, document uploading, status monitoring, announcement posting, notification delivery, interview scheduling, and record management.
The researchers conducted testing in several stages. First, individual modules of the system were checked to confirm that each feature worked correctly

on its own. These included user authentication, applicant profile management, application processing, document handling, and notification functions. Second, integration testing was performed to ensure that related modules worked properly when used together. For example, the researchers verified whether applicant registration correctly connected to profile creation, whether uploaded documents were linked to the correct application records, and whether status updates triggered the proper notifications. Lastly, overall system testing was carried out to assess the performance of the entire system in a simulated real-use environment.

In addition, usability testing was conducted to determine whether the system was easy to understand and operate for its intended users, particularly scholarship applicants, staff, and coordinators. The researchers observed how users navigated the system, completed tasks, and interpreted the interface. Minor issues such as confusing labels, navigation difficulties, or unclear instructions were noted for improvement. Security and access control were also checked to ensure that only authorized users could access restricted features and sensitive scholarship records.

Through this testing process, the researchers were able to identify errors, validate system functions, and confirm whether the proposed system was ready for implementation. The results of the testing served as the basis for refining the
system and ensuring that it could provide dependable support for the scholarship operations of the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental.

The Automated Scholarship Records Management System was evaluated to determine whether it met the intended functional and non-functional requirements of the study. The evaluation focused on the system’s ability to provide an organized, efficient, accurate, and user-friendly platform for managing scholarship applications and records in the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental. It also examined whether the system could support the needs of its intended users, particularly scholarship applicants, LGU staff, and scholarship coordinators.

The evaluation was based on how well the system performed its major functions, including applicant registration, OTP-based login verification, scholarship application processing, document uploading and monitoring, interview scheduling, notification delivery, status tracking, and scholarship record management. The researchers also considered the system’s usability, reliability, security, and overall responsiveness during actual use and simulated operations. These aspects were assessed to determine whether the system could consistently
support scholarship-related tasks with minimal errors and acceptable performance.

In addition, the evaluation examined the effectiveness of the system in reducing the difficulties commonly experienced in manual scholarship processing, such as delayed record retrieval, disorganized files, repetitive encoding, and slow dissemination of updates. Through the evaluation process, the researchers were able to determine whether the system could improve workflow efficiency, support better data organization, and provide a more convenient experience for both applicants and administrators.

The results of the evaluation served as the basis for identifying the strengths and limitations of the system. They also helped determine whether the proposed system was acceptable and suitable for implementation in the scholarship operations of the LGU of San Enrique. Overall, the evaluation provided evidence that the system can serve as a practical and reliable tool for improving scholarship records management.
The following are the key findings of the study based on the testing and evaluation of the Automated Scholarship Records Management System for the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental.

The system was found capable of performing its intended core functions. These include applicant registration, OTP-based verification, scholarship application submission, document uploading, application status monitoring, interview scheduling, announcement posting, notification delivery, and scholar record management. During system testing, these functions operated according to the intended workflow of the scholarship process and were able to support both applicant-side and administrator-side transactions.

In terms of record organization, the system was found to provide a more structured and centralized method of storing scholarship-related information. Applicant personal details, educational background, submitted requirements, application progress, and scholarship records were stored in a single database environment, making retrieval and monitoring more efficient compared to the previous manual process. This finding indicates that the system can help reduce the problem of scattered records and repetitive manual encoding.

The findings also showed that the application monitoring feature improved the tracking of applicants throughout the scholarship process. By using defined status levels such as Submitted, Initial Review, Pending Resubmission, For Interview, Eligible Awaiting SOA, Approved Pending Payroll, and Approved Finished, the system enabled staff to clearly determine the current standing of
each applicant. This made monitoring more systematic and reduced confusion in identifying incomplete, pending, or completed applications.
Another important finding of the study was the effectiveness of the document management feature. The system was able to link uploaded files, such as grades,

residency, and statement of account, to the appropriate application records. It was also found that the document status and versioning functions supported better monitoring of pending, verified, rejected, and resubmitted requirements. This helped improve document tracking and reduced the difficulty of reviewing scholarship requirements using purely manual procedures.

In terms of communication, the system was found to improve the dissemination of scholarship-related updates. Through OTP verification, in-system notifications, announcement posting, and SMS-based alerts, applicants were provided with more direct access to important information such as application updates, interview schedules, and other notices. This finding suggests that the system can lessen reliance on delayed or inconsistent manual announcement practices.

The study further found that the role-based access of the system supported better security and control over scholarship records. The distinction between student, staff, and administrator accounts ensured that access to sensitive

information and administrative functions was limited to authorized users only. The inclusion of audit logs, case notes, and notification records also strengthened accountability in system usage and transaction monitoring.
Overall, the findings of the study showed that the Automated Scholarship Records Management System

the scholarship management process of the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental. The system addressed major issues related to record organization, application monitoring, document tracking, and communication. Although it does not replace manual procedures such as physical document verification, accounting review, and actual fund release, it was found to be a functional and reliable support system for scholarship records management.

Based on the findings of the study, it is concluded that the Automated Scholarship Records Management System can effectively support the scholarship operations of the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental in a more organized, efficient, and systematic way. The system successfully carried out its intended functions, particularly in applicant registration, OTP-based verification, scholarship application processing, document uploading and monitoring, interview scheduling, notification delivery, and scholarship record management.

The study also concludes that the system was able to address several challenges found in the existing manual process. By centralizing applicant records, application details, document submissions, and status tracking, the system improved the organization and accessibility of scholarship-related information. It also created a clearer and more manageable workflow for monitoring applicants through the various stages of scholarship processing.

In addition, the study concludes that the inclusion of features such as document status monitoring, version tracking, announcements, SMS notifications, role-based access, case notes, and audit logs strengthened the system’s functionality and reliability. These features helped improve communication, accountability, and control in managing scholarship transactions and records.

However, it is also concluded that the system mainly serves as a support tool for scholarship records management and does not replace manual and government-required procedures such as physical document verification, accounting review, final approval, and the actual release of scholarship funds. Despite these limitations, the developed system was found to be a practical and dependable solution that can greatly improve the scholarship management process of the LGU.
Overall, the researchers conclude that the Automated Scholarship Records Management System is an acceptable and effective solution for managing

scholarship records and related processes in the LGU of San Enrique, Negros Occidental. Its implementation can help improve efficiency, strengthen record organization, and support more effective communication between the LGU and scholarship applicants.
Based on the study’s findings and conclusions, the following recommendations are presented.

The Local Government Unit (LGU) of San Enrique, Negros Occidental is encouraged to adopt the Automated Scholarship Records Management System as a support tool for handling scholarship applications, applicant information, document submissions, notifications, and other related transactions. Using the system may improve the efficiency, organization, and accessibility of scholarship operations compared to the current manual process.

It is also recommended that authorized LGU personnel, especially scholarship staff and coordinators, receive proper training before the system is fully implemented. Sufficient orientation and hands-on practice may help users better understand the system’s functions and reduce errors in data entry, status updates, and records management.

In addition, regular system maintenance and monitoring should be carried out after implementation. This should include periodic database backups, checking system performance, reviewing user access, and addressing any technical issues that may occur during actual use. Continuous monitoring may help maintain the system’s reliability, security, and long-term functionality.

The researchers further recommend the continued use of physical verification and government-required procedures alongside the digital system, particularly for official document validation, accounting review, auditing, final approval, and scholarship fund release. Since these processes are still beyond the scope of the developed application, proper coordination between manual and digital procedures remains important.

Lastly, future researchers are encouraged to enhance the system further by adding more advanced features such as online report generation, expanded analytics, automated qualification screening, email notifications, and wider interoperability for use in other local government units. Additional studies may also be conducted to improve the system’s scalability, usability, and overall functionality in similar institutional settings.
